_step0_note: A site dismissed at step 0 is NOT a scanner error. It is a site the rung has no question about, because no prior verdict existed for the branch to weaken.

entries.subject: langfuse
entries.why: `withInAppAgentToolApproval` marks every tool `requireApproval: true` EXCEPT those `isInAppAgentAutoApprovedToolName` accepts, so this predicate is the stage that removes a human approval gate from an agent's tool call. It is a principal waiver -- a name prefix, a local allowlist, and a role-derived `policy.autoApproved` set -- so the bound obligation is not engaged. The audit obligation is, and the module contains ZERO logging calls: nothing records that approval was skipped, so a reader of the agent's trace cannot distinguish a tool a human approved from one the policy waved through. The finding is the missing record, not the policy, which is a considered role-based design.

entries.subject: langfuse
entries.why: An operator-configured project id in `LANGFUSE_DELETE_SKIP_PROJECT_IDS` skips a deletion, which for a retention obligation is the permissive direction. A principal waiver, so the bound obligation is not engaged. The audit obligation is met in the same branch and in a strong form: the log names the rule that fired (`skipReason`), the project, the entity type, and every entity id skipped, so the waiver is not merely recorded but enumerable after the fact.

entries.subject: mastra
entries.why: `return null` from `handleDetectedPII` means 'no message modification', which the line's own comment says. The scanner read it as a benign verdict because the FUNCTION's name carries detection polarity and `null` is the permissive extreme for a risk-carrying name. The PII was detected; what is null is the rewrite. This shape accounts for 11 of this corpus's proposals and is the single largest false-positive class in it.

entries.subject: portkey-gateway
entries.why: In this codebase a plugin returns `{verdict, error, data}` and `verdict: false` means the check did not pass, so the write the scanner read as permissive is the DENY branch. The lexicon assumes low/false is the permissive extreme for a risk-carrying name; a subject whose verdict field is a pass/fail of the check rather than a level of risk inverts that assumption. This is a new false-positive mechanism, distinct from a polarity guess being wrong about a NAME, and it is reported as an instrument defect rather than patched mid-run.

entries.subject: promptfoo
entries.why: When the provider returned no guardrail data the assertion passes with `reason: 'Guardrail was not applied'`. That is 'the check did not run, so produce the safe value', which is the LIVENESS rung's question and not this one. Worth recording twice over: the domain classifier missed it because the falsiness test is on a value carried in the provider response rather than on a call made in this function, and the code itself discharges the trace obligation the liveness rung would ask about, because the reason string says the guardrail was not applied.

entries.subject: promptfoo
entries.why: `summary.sessionSkipped = true` when connectivity failed, on the line after a log saying exactly that. The liveness rung's question, and answered.

entries.subject: promptfoo
entries.why: An empty or missing `results` array from the moderation API maps to `{ flags: [] }`, i.e. nothing flagged, with no record. Same shape as the LlamaFirewall PII scanner the liveness rung owns in the Python corpus: an absent answer rendered as a clean one. Deferred, not counted, and named in the write-up because it is the more interesting of this subject's sites.

entries.subject: promptfoo
entries.why: `isAllowedCrossSite` returns true when origin and target are both loopback. This is the closest this corpus came to a second finding and we declined it: the condition is a structural fact about the two hostnames rather than a verdict being weakened, and a local development server treating localhost-to-localhost as same-site is the documented intent. Recorded as declined rather than omitted, because a reader may weigh it differently.

entries.subject: retire.js
entries.why: `options.insecure` sets `rejectUnauthorized = false` on every advisory download, disabling TLS certificate verification for the channel the scanner's own evidence arrives on. A principal waiver, so the BOUND obligation is not engaged. The AUDIT obligation is, and nothing records it: the only other occurrences of `insecure` in the package are the CLI flag's declaration and its type. The run prints its findings without stating that the advisories behind them were fetched over an unverified channel, so a reader of a clean report cannot tell which kind of clean it is.

entries.why: CSS/AST predicates and parsing helpers -- `isValid`, `isBlocklessAtRuleAfterSameNameBlocklessAtRule`, `findAnimationName` -- each of which computes the answer it returns rather than weakening an earlier one. `findAnimationName` is the interesting exception and is named rather than buried: it sets `shouldBeIgnored = true` and empties `animationNames` when the value uses non-standard syntax, which is 'the analysis could not run, so produce the safe empty result'. That is the LIVENESS rung's question, not this one, and it is reported here for the same reason 72 sites were deferred in the Python corpus. The two suppression-layer modules in this directory are read individually and are matched before this rule

entries.subject: stylelint
entries.why: `result.warnings = result.warnings.filter(...)` drops a rule's warnings ONLY under `problemsCount <= suppressionsCount`. That is the bound obligation met in a quantitative form stronger than any site in the Python corpus: the relaxation consults a magnitude of the evidence it overrides against an operator-committed count, and if the problems exceed the count NOTHING is suppressed and every problem is reported. The audit obligation is met at the system level rather than at the site -- the committed suppressions file is itself the record of what may be suppressed, and the function returns the `unused` remainder so a stale baseline is visible. The same system-level reading was applied to detect-secrets in the Python corpus and is applied here for the same reason.
